key_decisions.decision: Retains the location and unequal silver and gold amounts; explains the imposed payment through levy.
Preserves the purpose clause without asserting here that the proposed deportation happened.
Keeps the partial removal and palace/temple ambiguity in a note on hekal.
Retains the pinned Hebrew age eight and the precise duration; notes the difference from Kings rather than harmonizing.
Retains the Hebrew brother relationship in the text and explains the uncle relationship in Kings separately.
Preserves the oath and both bodily images, with returning connected to the book’s recurring language.
Renders the repeated early sending idiom as persistent action and keeps compassion as the stated reason.
Keeps the sanctuary killing and differentiated victims explicit; makes the agents readable without softening the violence.
Makes the captives’ subjection explicit while keeping its stated endpoint.
Retains the land’s Sabbath image and seventy years without importing a harmonized chronology.
Retains Cyrus’s sweeping royal claim and ends with the source’s invitation to go up, leaving the return ahead.
